classification.difficultyReason: Sketch two principal inverse trigonometric graphs and add their ordinates to identify a constant sum.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Sketch $y=\sin^{-1}x$ and $y=\cos^{-1}x$ on the same set of axes.

spec.description: Portrait coordinate scaffold shared by both parts; double-ended axes, no grid or origin label.
spec.mathematics: Horizontal ticks at -1 and 1; vertical ticks at -pi/2, pi/2 and pi.
spec.answerVisibility: Axes and ticks remain visible; all three answer curves are hidden.

answer.short: See the shared graph: inverse sine is blue and inverse cosine is red.
answer.worked: Sketch the increasing inverse-sine curve through $(-1,-\frac{\pi}{2})$, $(0,0)$ and $(1,\frac{\pi}{2})$. Sketch the decreasing inverse-cosine curve through $(-1,\pi)$, $(0,\frac{\pi}{2})$ and $(1,0)$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: By adding ordinates, sketch the graph of $y=\sin^{-1}x+\cos^{-1}x$.

answer.short: $y=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ for $-1\le x\le1$; see the purple segment on the shared graph.
answer.worked:
Adding the ordinates of the two curves gives $\frac{\pi}{2}$ at every common abscissa. For example,
$$\begin{aligned}
x=-1:&\quad -\frac{\pi}{2}+\pi=\frac{\pi}{2}\\
x=0:&\quad 0+\frac{\pi}{2}=\frac{\pi}{2}\\
x=1:&\quad \frac{\pi}{2}+0=\frac{\pi}{2}.
\end{aligned}$$
Sketch the horizontal segment $y=\frac{\pi}{2}$ from $x=-1$ to $x=1$, including both endpoints.

spec.description: Both inverse curves and their ordinate sum share one coordinate frame. No curve labels or explicit endpoint markers are printed.
spec.mathematics: Blue y=arcsin(x), red y=arccos(x), and purple y=pi/2, all on [-1,1]. Curves are plotted parametrically from their defining trigonometric functions.
